q: How much CO2 does silicon carbide production emit per tonne?
title: Silicon carbide CO2 per tonne
short: Two parts: process CO2 from the petroleum coke that reduces the silica, for which IPCC 2006 gives a default of about 2.62 t CO2 per tonne of silicon carbide, and the large electricity use of the Acheson furnace at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh.
audience: Silicon carbide and abrasive grain producers

ul: Silica sand and petroleum coke react in the furnace; the carbon leaves as CO that burns to CO2.
Measure coke input and its carbon content for a plant figure; use the IPCC default only if you have nothing better.

p: Each furnace run draws power for hours. Use the furnace meter per batch and divide by tonnes of crude silicon carbide recovered.
Silicon carbide is not a CBAM good. EU buyers may still ask for a figure for their own Scope 3.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative figures)
lines: Output: 1,000 tonnes of silicon carbide in a year.
Process CO2 at the IPCC default: 1,000 × 2.62 = 2,620 t CO2.
Furnace electricity is added on top from the meter.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
